correctness.rationale: For any compactly supported invariant probability measure the slow increment Δy=-μ(x-(σ−1)) has zero mean, giving E[x]=σ−1. Stationarity of y² expands to 0=−2μ Cov(x,y)+μ² Var(x), hence Cov=(μ/2)Var(x); no fast-map regularity is required. Cauchy–Schwarz gives the sharp variance lower bound. Equality with nonzero Var(x) fixes y−Ey=(μ/2)(x−m) almost surely, and invariance applies this relation at the image point, so x_{n+1}−m=−(x_n−m), y_{n+2}=y_n a.s.; any ergodic nondegenerate equality measure is a two-cycle. The strict correlation assertion correctly excludes zero Var(x), fixed points and period-two equality. Independent hand expansion and exact-rational source-code inspection confirm normalization μ=.001, σ=.322.

value.rationale: Stationary fast–slow covariance is a natural physical statistic for the canonical Rulkov neuron map. The result gives an exact global consistency law and fluctuation bound across all compact stationary regimes and, crucially, converts equality in a statistical bound into a dynamical period-two obstruction. That motivated structural rigidity exceeds a trivial normalizing observation and is independently useful for comparing simulated regular versus bursting invariant statistics.

scientific_limitations: Compactly supported invariant Borel probabilities only; no existence or uniqueness of chaotic invariant measures is established.
Equal covariance determinant with Var(x)>0 forces support on period≤2 points a.s.; a nonergodic mixture is not necessarily a single 2-cycle.
Result asserts no quantitative prediction for higher moments or all return-time statistics.
